intended_object: The standard surjective algebra map Π_k(Q) → kQ, from the preprojective algebra of a finite quiver Q onto its path algebra. It kills every reverse arrow a* and fixes the vertex idempotents and the arrows of Q. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body uses `preprojectiveLift` to push `symmetrifyRetraction` down to the quotient. `symmetrifyRetraction` is the k-algebra map from the path algebra of the doubled quiver to kQ that sends a doubled path to itself when it uses only arrows of Q, and to 0 otherwise. The proof that it kills the relator ρ = ∑ₐ (a a* − a* a) is correct: every term contains a reverse arrow, so its image is 0, and the map therefore factors through Π_k(Q). This is exactly the standard quotient map from Crawley-Boevey and Ringel. The library also shows that it is a left inverse of the inclusion kQ → Π_k(Q), which confirms the intended behaviour.

On generality: k only needs to be a commutative ring, which is the natural setting. The finiteness assumptions (`Fintype Q` and finitely many arrows between any two vertices) are what makes the relator a finite sum, so the preprojective algebra itself needs them; they are not an unnecessary restriction. Mathlib has no preprojective algebras or quiver path algebras, so there is no counterpart.
